question: Which type of study collects data at just one single point in time?

options.A: Longitudinal study
options.B: Experimental trial
options.C: Cross-sectional study
options.D: Prospective cohort study

explanation: You've got this! A cross-sectional study is like taking a quick photograph—it gathers all the data from people at one specific moment.

question: What is the medicalisation of FGM?

options.A: Using modern local anesthesia during traditional FGM rites
options.B: Performing FGM using trained healthcare workers in clinical settings
options.C: Treating the physical complications of FGM in a hospital
options.D: Researching surgical ways to reverse FGM damage

explanation: Medicalisation refers to health professionals performing the procedure under the false assumption that clinical hygiene removes the harm. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is the primary characteristic that makes skeletal muscle different from smooth muscle?

options.A: It is found exclusively inside blood vessel walls
options.B: It lacks any visible striations under a microscope
options.C: It can contract entirely without any nerve supply
options.D: It is under voluntary conscious control

explanation: Skeletal muscle is consciously controlled by the somatic nervous system, unlike smooth muscle which works automatically. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h1)

question: What major health threat usually pops up first when clean water supplies and sewage systems break down during a disaster?

options.A: Waterborne disease outbreaks like cholera
options.B: Widespread Vitamin D deficiency
options.C: Chronic bone fractures
options.D: Sudden increases in genetic disorders

explanation: When sewage mixes with drinking water, tummy troubles and deadly infections like cholera follow fast. Safe water is lifesaving!

question: What is the most frequent cause of heavy bleeding after an abortion?

options.A: Severe high blood pressure
options.B: An allergic reaction to antibiotics
options.C: Retained products of conception
options.D: A sudden drop in body temperature

explanation: When tiny bits of tissue are left behind in the uterus, the muscle cannot clamp down tight to stop the bleeding. Always suspect retained tissue when heavy bleeding happens!

question: Why are some oral tablets manufactured with an enteric coating?

options.A: To protect the stomach lining and prevent the drug from dissolving too early
options.B: To combine two different drugs into a single dose
options.C: To help the medicine dissolve instantly in the mouth
options.D: To make the pill taste sweet for young children

explanation: Enteric-coated drugs are designed to pass through the acidic stomach unharmed and only dissolve once they reach the small intestine. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of the National Programme on Immunization?

options.A: Treating chronic non-communicable illnesses in adults
options.B: Supplying essential nutrition supplements to pregnant women
options.C: Protecting populations from vaccine-preventable diseases
options.D: Providing free surgical care for newborn congenital defects

explanation: The NPI focuses specifically on preventing infectious diseases through safe and effective vaccination schedules. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h1)

question: How is a purpose statement different from a problem statement?

options.A: The problem statement contains all the final conclusions
options.B: The problem statement is written after data is collected
options.C: The purpose statement only lists financial costs
options.D: The purpose statement declares the direct aim or goal of the study

explanation: While the problem statement highlights the trouble or gap, the purpose statement tells us what your study specifically plans to do about it.

question: Why does a full bladder often make postpartum bleeding worse?

options.A: It blocks the release of oxytocin from the brain
options.B: It causes severe high blood pressure in the mother
options.C: It pushes the uterus upward and stops it from contracting
options.D: It dilutes the clotting factors in the bloodstream

explanation: Fantastic! A full bladder pushes the uterus out of place so the muscles can't squeeze tightly around those open blood vessels. Always remember to check the bladder!

question: How do relaxation and distraction techniques help reduce a patient's pain?

options.A: They destroy nociceptor nerves in the skin
options.B: They permanently change pain chemicals in the blood
options.C: They stop the liver from breaking down pain meds
options.D: They trigger nerve pathways that block pain signals at the spinal cord

explanation: Think of the 'gate control theory'—calming or distracting activities send fast signals along big nerve fibers that close the spinal gate before pain signals can reach the brain.

question: When should discharge planning ideally start in primary nursing?

options.A: When the patient complains about high hospital bills
options.B: Right upon the patient's admission to the unit
options.C: Only after the doctor signs the official discharge papers
options.D: On the exact morning the patient is scheduled to leave

explanation: Smart nursing! We start planning for home the very minute the patient walks through the door so nothing is rushed at the end.

question: What is the main goal of post-abortion care (PAC)?

options.A: To investigate the legal cause of pregnancy termination
options.B: To treat complications from spontaneous or induced abortions
options.C: To perform mandatory psychological evaluations
options.D: To provide routine family planning counseling only

explanation: PAC is all about emergency medical support! It focuses on treating physical issues like heavy bleeding or infections so the patient can recover safely.

question: Which bone forms the large, flared upper part of the hip bone?

options.A: Ilium
options.B: Coccyx
options.C: Pubis
options.D: Ischium

explanation: The ilium is the broad, upper fan-shaped section of the hip bone that you feel on your waist. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h1)

question: Where is the correct spot to inject an emergency epinephrine auto-injector?

options.A: The soft skin directly over the abdomen
options.B: The upper fatty tissue of the arm
options.C: The large muscle of the buttocks
options.D: The outer middle thigh muscle

explanation: Spot on! The outer middle thigh (anterolateral thigh) has great muscle and blood flow for the fastest drug absorption during an emergency.

question: What key lifestyle advice should a nurse include when educating a patient with prediabetes?

options.A: Avoid all types of physical movement to preserve energy
options.B: Sleep for at least fourteen hours every single night
options.C: Incorporate a balanced diet and regular physical activity
options.D: Eliminate all forms of water from the daily diet

explanation: Dietary changes and regular exercise help improve insulin sensitivity and prevent prediabetes from advancing to full diabetes. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h9)

question: A patient with advanced kidney disease has high potassium levels in their blood. Which local fruit should you advise them to limit?

options.A: Plain clear water and herbal tea
options.B: Unsalted butter and cooking oils
options.C: Ripe bananas and fresh oranges
options.D: White refined flour and table sugar

explanation: Bananas and oranges are loaded with potassium! When the kidneys aren't working well, extra potassium can cause dangerous heart rhythm problems. Always good to know.

question: Why is practicing injection safety a core professional duty for every nurse?

options.A: Because patients will refuse treatment if nurses lack safety gear
options.B: Because drug manufacturers mandate strict handling instructions
options.C: Because hospital management requires paperwork for every needle used
options.D: Because handling needles always carries a potential window for exposure and infection

explanation: You handle sharps every single day on the ward. Knowing safety rules protects your own health just as much as it protects your patients!

question: A patient is dealing with loneliness and money troubles after losing their partner. What do these life events represent?

options.A: Genetic and chromosomal mutations
options.B: Environmental and situational stressors
options.C: Primary endocrine abnormalities
options.D: Congenital brain structural defects

explanation: You nailed it! Things happening in a person's surroundings—like loss, isolation, or financial stress—are situational triggers that can spark depression.

question: Why must a nurse verify insurance authorization before certain hospital procedures?

options.A: To prevent the patient from speaking with doctors
options.B: To ensure the HMO will cover the cost of the treatment
options.C: To calculate the personal salary of the hospital accountant
options.D: To update the national census database immediately

explanation: HMOs require prior authorization for specialized procedures so that the hospital is guaranteed reimbursement for services rendered. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h7)

question: During an infection, a patient feels generally tired and off before specific symptoms appear. What is this early stage called?

options.A: Prodromal period
options.B: Incubation period
options.C: Convalescent period
options.D: Illness period

explanation: Spot on! The prodromal phase is that 'coming down with something' feeling—just general tiredness or malaise before the main symptoms hit.

question: Which special cells form the only output pathway leaving the cerebellar cortex?

options.A: Basket cells
options.B: Granule cells
options.C: Purkinje cells
options.D: Stellate cells

explanation: Purkinje cells are those iconic, large neurons with huge dendritic trees. Their axons provide the final (and inhibitory) output from the cerebellar cortex down to the deep nuclei. Keep up the amazing work!

question: What is the main reason nurses and planners must set priorities?

options.A: Healthcare resources are always limited
options.B: All health problems cost the exact same amount to treat
options.C: Government policies forbid buying new medical equipment
options.D: Doctors refuse to participate in budgeting meetings

explanation: That's right! Since funds, drugs, and hands are never endless, we have to choose which urgent needs to tackle first.

question: What is the most immediate, life-threatening danger for a mother with a placental abnormality?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Postpartum depression
options.C: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: Urinary tract infection

explanation: When the placenta doesn't attach or separate normally, the womb often struggles to clamp down afterward, leading to heavy, dangerous bleeding. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h7)

question: What is the main goal of doing a secondary survey in critical care?

options.A: To administer routine scheduled morning drugs
options.B: To uncover hidden injuries or underlying problems
options.C: To discharge the patient from the hospital ward
options.D: To replace the need for laboratory blood tests

explanation: The head-to-toe secondary exam helps you find any sneaky injuries or issues that might have hidden during the fast primary survey.

question: What is the primary calming chemical messenger (inhibitory neurotransmitter) targeted by most sleeping pills?

options.A: Dopamine
options.B: Norepinephrine
options.C: Acetylcholine
options.D: Gamma-aminobutyric acid

explanation: GABA (Gamma-aminobutyric acid) is your brain's natural brake pedal. Sedatives and hypnotics step down hard on this pedal to help the brain relax.

question: Why is teaching new staff about infection control only on their first day not enough?

options.A: Hospital management changes policies every single week without fail
options.B: New nurses never listen to instructions given on their first day
options.C: Good habits fade and new safety guidelines emerge over time
options.D: Trainees are not allowed to touch patients until their second year

explanation: You got it! Regular refreshers keep safety fresh in everyone's mind as new guidelines come out.

question: A virus is hiding safely inside body cells. Which part of the immune system handles this best?

options.A: The complement protein cascade in the blood plasma
options.B: Innate physical barriers of the skin and mucous membranes
options.C: Humoral immunity via circulating antibodies
options.D: Cell-mediated immunity via cytotoxic T-cells

explanation: Correct! When germs hide inside cells, cytotoxic T-cells are the hit squad that hunts down and destroys those infected cells.

question: What is a major perk of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) compared to warfarin?

options.A: They use fixed dosing without routine lab monitoring
options.B: They can be easily reversed with green leafy vegetables
options.C: They have no risk of bleeding complications
options.D: They require daily blood tests for safety

explanation: DOACs are super convenient because patients take a standard pill without needing constant needle pricks for lab tests. Brilliant!

question: What is the main goal of gerontological nursing?

options.A: Emergency surgical interventions
options.B: Pediatric development milestones
options.C: Curative treatment for infectious diseases
options.D: Care of older adults and healthy aging

explanation: You've got this! Gerontological nursing is all about helping older adults live healthy, comfortable lives while managing long-term conditions. It's caring for the elderly with dignity.

question: Why do public health educators emphasize hand hygiene and washing vegetables?

options.A: To stop bacteria from causing secondary cyst infections
options.B: To eliminate adult tapeworms living in human intestines
options.C: To remove lingering agricultural pesticides from produce
options.D: To prevent the accidental ingestion of microscopic parasite eggs

explanation: Good washing habits wash away those tiny dog-shed eggs before they can enter our mouths.

question: A nurse wants to promote exclusive breastfeeding in a community where older women traditionally give infants water. What is the most culturally sensitive first step?

options.A: Threaten mothers with heavy fines if they give water to babies
options.B: Engage respected grandmothers to discuss modern infant nutrition benefits
options.C: Ignore the grandmothers and focus only on teenage girls
options.D: Print posters in English warning that local grandmothers are dangerous

explanation: Grandmothers are powerful influencers in our communities! Bringing them on board as allies rather than fighting them is a mark of smart, respectful nursing practice.

question: Why are traditional media like village drama troupes and town criers so effective in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: They use familiar cultural formats that local people easily relate to
options.B: They require expensive electricity and satellite dishes
options.C: They are the only legal way to share health messages
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for trained nurses

explanation: Exactly! When you meet people through their own cultural practices like drama and town criers, they naturally tune in and trust the message. Great public health intuition!

question: How do the different types of viral hepatitis mainly differ from one another?

options.A: Only Hepatitis A and B cause physical symptoms, while the rest are completely harmless
options.B: Each type is caused by a distinct virus with unique transmission routes and clinical outcomes
options.C: They all share the exact same transmission route through contaminated food and water
options.D: They are all different stages of the exact same viral infection progressing over time

explanation: Think of Hepatitis A through E as a family of completely separate viruses. Each one behaves differently, spreads in its own way, and affects the body differently.

question: How can data from a patient's wearable device assist the nursing staff?

options.A: By ordering hospital meals based on step counts
options.B: By prescribing medication without a doctor's signature
options.C: By showing early warning signs like an unusual rise in resting heart rate
options.D: By diagnosing complex mental health disorders automatically

explanation: Continuous tracking on wearables can alert nurses to subtle physiological changes before a patient's condition deteriorates severely. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h5)

question: A home health nurse notices signs of severe postpartum depression during a visit. What is the best collaborative action?

options.A: Wait until the baby is one year old before mentioning the concern.
options.B: Tell the family that mood changes always resolve completely on their own.
options.C: Refer the mother to a mental health specialist or social worker promptly.
options.D: Prescribe an antidepressant medication during the home visit.

explanation: Involving mental health professionals and social workers ensures the patient receives safe, specialized support for postpartum mood disorders. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h8)

question: Why is it actually helpful for bedside nurses to understand basic health economics?

options.A: It helps them appreciate the operational challenges of resource allocation and patient flow
options.B: It prevents patients from ever experiencing chronic illnesses in the community
options.C: It allows them to negotiate direct commission fees for prescribing medications
options.D: It removes the need for doctors to write formal treatment orders

explanation: Spot on! Knowing economics helps you understand why management makes certain staffing decisions and how best to manage patient beds on your ward.

question: An HIV-positive mum looks worried and stressed about her infant feeding choices. What should be your very first step as a student nurse?

options.A: Build trust and provide a safe space to discuss her fears and questions
options.B: Tell her immediately that formula feeding is the only acceptable choice
options.C: Hand her a detailed textbook on virology and let her read independently
options.D: Involve her extended family in the discussion without her prior consent

explanation: Wonderful nursing instinct! Always start by creating a warm, judgment-free space where she feels safe to share her worries before diving into clinical advice.

question: Which ventilator mode gives a set volume when the patient tries to breathe, but also guarantees a minimum backup rate if they get too tired?

options.A: Control mode
options.B: Assist-Control mode
options.C: Continuous Positive Airway Pressure
options.D: Pressure Support mode

explanation: In Assist-Control mode, the machine is always watching: if the patient breathes, the machine helps out with a full breath. If the patient stops trying, the machine's timer steps in to breathe for them!

question: Why are doctors and nurses careful about giving strong pain relief right away to someone with undiagnosed, severe belly pain?

options.A: Analgesics always cure appendicitis without an operation
options.B: Patients with stomach pain cannot swallow pills
options.C: Pain medicines cause immediate kidney failure
options.D: It can mask important physical signs and delay necessary surgery

explanation: Good clinical thinking! Masking the pain can hide how the illness is progressing, making it tricky for surgeons to figure out what's really wrong inside.

question: Which of these is NOT a sign that a patient is lacking fluid (fluid volume deficit)?

options.A: Poor skin turgor
options.B: Dry mucous membranes
options.C: Bounding peripheral pulses
options.D: Concentrated dark urine

explanation: You're doing great! Bounding pulses mean there is plenty of fluid pumping around (or too much!). Dehydration actually causes weak, thready pulses.

question: Why can mechanical ventilation sometimes cause a patient's blood pressure to drop?

options.A: The ventilator directly causes vasodilation of peripheral arteries
options.B: Increased chest pressure reduces blood return to the heart
options.C: Sedative medications increase the heart rate too much
options.D: High oxygen levels make blood vessels constrict sharply

explanation: Pumping positive air pressure into the chest creates a tight squeeze around the heart's main blood vessels, making it a bit harder for blood to flow back to the heart temporarily.

question: What should a patient with a respiratory infection wear when moving outside their isolation room?

options.A: Cover the patient completely with a sterile plastic sheet
options.B: Transport the patient only during night shift hours
options.C: Ensure the patient walks without any staff assistance
options.D: Have the patient wear a surgical mask during transport

explanation: Exactly! Having the patient wear a mask traps any stray respiratory droplets right at the source while you walk them through the hospital corridors.

question: Why is it tricky that many STIs in women show no symptoms at all?

options.A: The immune system permanently attacks healthy tissues instead of the pathogen
options.B: Infected women unknowingly spread the infection and delay necessary treatment
options.C: Routine diagnostic tests consistently fail to detect silent infections
options.D: Asymptomatic infections immediately progress to systemic organ failure

explanation: When an infection causes no signs or pain, a woman has no reason to visit the clinic, letting the disease grow quietly and pass to others.

question: How does the school use overall performance data from an entire class?

options.A: To spot gaps in the curriculum and update courses
options.B: To decide who gets scholarship money
options.C: To market the school to new applicants
options.D: To cut down the required clinical hours

explanation: When schools look at how everyone scored as a group, they can see if a certain course needs better materials or extra teaching time.

question: What should you do if you notice sudden joint swelling and severe redness during an exercise session?

options.A: Cover the swollen joint with a heavy blanket and leave
options.B: Stop the exercise, report to the doctor, and document it
options.C: Massage the swollen area firmly with rubbing alcohol
options.D: Keep exercising faster to break up the swelling

explanation: Well done! Sudden swelling or redness means you need to pause right away, let the doctor know, and chart what happened.

question: Why do many young women and teenagers in Nigeria end up turning to unsafe abortion methods?

options.A: Preference for traditional herbal remedies over modern medicine
options.B: Easy availability of safe surgical clinics in rural areas
options.C: Lack of financial resources and reproductive health access
options.D: Strict enforcement of mandatory hospital reporting laws

explanation: Poverty, fear of social stigma, and struggling to find safe, legal services often push vulnerable girls into dangerous alternatives. As nurses, keeping our clinics open and welcoming is key to changing this.

question: What is the primary purpose of Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM)?

options.A: To force every patient to visit the hospital daily
options.B: To track patient vital signs from their home using digital devices
options.C: To store paper records in a warehouse far from the clinic
options.D: To replace human nurses with automated computer screens

explanation: RPM sends real-time health data like blood pressure or sugar levels from the patient's house straight to the healthcare team. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the main goal of using triage protocols during a mass casualty event?

options.A: To assign patients to private rooms for maximum personal comfort
options.B: To ensure that patients are treated strictly in the order they arrived
options.C: To collect personal financial and insurance data from every victim
options.D: To categorize victims based on clinical urgency and survival probability

explanation: Triage lets responders quickly spot who needs immediate life-saving care versus who can wait safely.

question: Which of these is a social and cultural concept rather than a purely biological one?

options.A: Anatomical organs
options.B: Gender
options.C: Chromosomes
options.D: Hormone levels

explanation: Well done! Gender involves societal roles and identities, while chromosomes and physical organs are purely biological.

question: Why do we advise pregnant mothers to eat small, frequent meals instead of three massive plates of food?

options.A: To prevent sudden drops in blood sugar during the afternoon
options.B: To speed up the absorption of prenatal vitamins into the bloodstream
options.C: To prevent the stomach from becoming overly full and putting pressure on the sphincter
options.D: To stop the liver from producing excess bile during digestion

explanation: Smaller meals keep tummy pressure low, stopping acid from splashing up into the food pipe.

question: An elderly patient with poor eyesight and mild forgetfulness is prescribed a new blood pressure pill. What is your best nursing strategy to help them remember?

options.A: Hand over a dense medical journal article explaining the drug's mechanism
options.B: Instruct a family member to administer the pills without involving the patient
options.C: Provide large-print written instructions and suggest a pill organizer box
options.D: Tell the patient to memorize the dosing schedule without any external aids

explanation: Spot on! Practical tools like big print and pill boxes make managing medications at home much easier and safer for older adults.

question: When is a patient usually considered for epilepsy surgery?

options.A: Only when the patient refuses to take any pills at all
options.B: Immediately upon receiving the first diagnosis of a seizure
options.C: When seizures persist despite trying multiple appropriate medications
options.D: When the electroencephalogram shows a normal brain pattern

explanation: Surgery is saved for drug-resistant cases where standard medications have been tried properly but still haven't stopped the seizures. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h6)

question: What is the medical term for an infection in the muscular middle layer of the heart?

options.A: Endocarditis
options.B: Myocarditis
options.C: Pericarditis
options.D: Epicarditis

explanation: You've got this! 'Myo' means muscle, and 'itis' means inflammation. So myocarditis is simply inflammation of the heart muscle. Keep up the great work!

question: In which lobe of the brain is the primary touch (somatosensory) cortex found?

options.A: Temporal lobe
options.B: Parietal lobe
options.C: Frontal lobe
options.D: Occipital lobe

explanation: You've got this! The parietal lobe sits right at the top-back of your brain and is the main station for processing everything you touch.

question: Why is teamwork across different sectors necessary when addressing the health needs of unemployed persons?

options.A: Joblessness affects multiple aspects of life that healthcare alone cannot fix
options.B: Medical clinics have unlimited funds for business startups
options.C: Nurses are legally forbidden from talking to social workers
options.D: Government agencies prefer to work in complete isolation

explanation: Correct! Unemployment involves housing, food, and financial needs that require teamwork across different community sectors. Well done! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h7)

question: What is a notable disadvantage of topical drug administration?

options.A: It is impossible to use if the patient has a functioning gastrointestinal tract
options.B: Absorption can be unpredictable due to skin thickness and condition
options.C: It causes immediate and severe first-pass liver failure every time
options.D: It always requires sterile operating room conditions to apply

explanation: Because skin condition, hydration, and thickness vary across the body and between patients, absorption rates can be inconsistent. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h5)

question: Which of the following is a common physical sign frequently experienced by a grieving person?

options.A: Permanent loss of hearing
options.B: High fever and skin rashes
options.C: Extreme fatigue and sleep changes
options.D: Sudden increase in muscle mass

explanation: Grief heavily drains physical energy, frequently causing profound fatigue and trouble sleeping. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h4)

question: What must a birth attendant do if a sterile item from the kit accidentally falls onto the floor?

options.A: Spray it with alcohol before using
options.B: Discard or replace the item immediately
options.C: Use it only if the floor looks dry
options.D: Wipe it clean with the kit soap and water

explanation: Once a sterile item touches the floor, its sterility is permanently compromised and it cannot be made safe for use again. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h5)

question: Why are visual aids and practical demonstrations useful during health counseling in primary care?

options.A: They replace the need for the nurse to speak at all
options.B: They make health messages easier to understand for people with varying literacy levels
options.C: They ensure patients never forget a single word of advice
options.D: They make the clinic look more modern and well-equipped

explanation: Visuals and demonstrations bridge literacy gaps and make abstract health concepts concrete and memorable. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T12#GNS124_U5_T12_h6)

question: How does a typical resting tremor look in a patient with early Parkinson's disease?

options.A: As rhythmic head nodding that worsens only during high-stress situations
options.B: As violent shaking of both arms when reaching out to grab an object
options.C: As a pill-rolling movement of the thumb and forefinger when the hand is relaxed
options.D: As sudden muscle jerks throughout the entire body during deep sleep

explanation: Picture someone gently rolling a tiny pill back and forth between their thumb and index finger while resting—that's the classic Parkinson's resting tremor!

question: A woman receiving an oxytocin drip shows severe late decelerations on her CTG. What is the most appropriate immediate nursing action?

options.A: Discontinue the oxytocin infusion immediately
options.B: Ask the mother to walk around the ward
options.C: Wait for thirty minutes to see if the pattern improves
options.D: Increase the oxytocin drip to speed up delivery

explanation: Stopping oxytocin removes the stimulus for contractions, giving the uterus a chance to rest and restore blood flow to the placenta. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h5)

question: Why is comprehensive sexuality education more effective than just telling teens to practice abstinence?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for any clinical health assessments
options.B: It encourages immediate experimentation with hazardous behaviors
options.C: It equips them with practical safety information, consent knowledge, and contraceptive options
options.D: It eliminates all biological urges in developing adolescents

explanation: Spot on! Giving young people real-world safety tools and knowledge empowers them to make healthier, informed choices.

question: What name did Casimir Funk originally give to essential food factors that he believed were life-giving amines?

options.A: Macronutrients
options.B: Electrolytes
options.C: Vitamines
options.D: Caloric units

explanation: That's correct! He combined 'vital' and 'amines' to coin the term 'vitamines' for these crucial health-boosting substances.

question: Which of these symptoms is a classic danger sign that could mean a pregnant woman is developing pre-eclampsia?

options.A: Mild swelling of the fingers in the morning
options.B: Occasional lower back pain
options.C: Severe headache and blurred vision
options.D: Increased appetite for sweet foods

explanation: Severe headaches and changes in vision are big red flags for dangerously high blood pressure (pre-eclampsia). Always take this seriously!

question: Which skin preparation practice is essential before performing an intraarticular puncture?

options.A: Applying warm lotion to soften the skin surface
options.B: Shaving the entire limb hair without any cleanser
options.C: Wiping the skin clean with a dry cotton ball only
options.D: Allowing the antiseptic solution to dry completely on the skin

explanation: Antiseptic agents need time to dry so they can fully kill microbes on the skin surface before the needle enters. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h6)

question: If a patient's hands have a fine, gentle tremble during a quick physical check, what might this point to?

options.A: Hypothyroidism
options.B: Fluid overload
options.C: Hyperthyroidism
options.D: Adrenal suppression

explanation: When the thyroid is in overdrive (hyperthyroidism), it speeds up your metabolism and makes the nervous system super jittery, which often shows up as shaky hands.

question: If a patient shows clear signs of shock after eating an allergen, which classic symptom might actually be completely missing?

options.A: Severe stomach cramps
options.B: Swelling of the tongue
options.C: Hives or skin rashes
options.D: Difficulty breathing

explanation: Surprise! Up to 20% of severe anaphylaxis cases don't show any skin rashes or hives. Never rule out anaphylaxis just because the skin looks clear.

question: An unconscious accident victim is rushed in. What legal concept allows you to give emergency care without their verbal consent?

options.A: Expressed consent
options.B: Mandatory consent
options.C: Informed consent
options.D: Implied consent

explanation: You got it! When a patient can't speak and their life is in danger, the law assumes ('implies') they would want you to save their life.

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse should tell a patient being treated for infectious cervicitis?

options.A: Use barrier methods consistently to help prevent reinfection.
options.B: Make sure your sexual partner is treated at the same time.
options.C: Stop taking your medicine as soon as the discharge lessens.
options.D: Avoid having sex until your treatment is fully completed.

explanation: Never advise stopping meds early just because symptoms fade. They must finish the entire course!

question: What is the main job of glucose inside Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS)?

options.A: It masks the salty taste of the solution for infants
options.B: It slows down the movement of food through the stomach
options.C: It provides all the daily calories a sick child needs
options.D: It helps transport sodium and water across the intestinal wall

explanation: It's like a buddy system! Glucose hitches a ride with sodium and water, pulling them across the intestinal wall back into the bloodstream to stop dehydration.

question: A nurse sees imported vaccines with broken safety seals. Which agency should be alerted immediately?

options.A: The Nigerian Police Force
options.B: National Bureau of Statistics
options.C: NAFDAC
options.D: NMCN

explanation: Great thinking! NAFDAC is our national watchdog for checking the safety and quality of drugs, vaccines, and medical products coming into the country.

question: Why is using a shared conceptual framework useful for spreading evidence-based practice?

options.A: It stops nurses from asking questions about new procedures
options.B: It provides a standard language for discussing patient outcomes
options.C: It removes the need for patient consent during studies
options.D: It makes clinical guidelines completely optional for staff

explanation: When all nurses speak the same clinical language, it is much easier to share what works and improve patient care together.

question: What does a sudden, significant drop in the baby's heart rate during a contraction usually suggest?

options.A: fetal distress or cord compression
options.B: rapid progression to the second stage
options.C: normal physiological sleep cycles
options.D: maternal exhaustion and dehydration

explanation: Spot on. Big dips in heart rate can mean the baby isn't getting enough oxygen, often due to cord pressure or distress.

question: Which symptoms point straight to acute food poisoning?

options.A: Progressive swelling of the lower legs
options.B: Persistent dry cough and hoarseness
options.C: Sudden vomiting and abdominal cramps
options.D: Gradual loss of long-term memory

explanation: Your stomach and intestines will react fast and violently to bad toxins, leading to sudden cramps and throwing up.

question: What naturally happens to a pregnant woman's blood (plasma) volume during normal gestation?

options.A: It increases significantly
options.B: It remains completely unchanged
options.C: It decreases by half
options.D: It drops to zero temporarily

explanation: Plasma volume expands greatly during pregnancy to supply the placenta and keep up with the body's new demands. Amazing how the body adapts!

question: What is considered the single most effective way to stop the spread of infections in a hospital?

options.A: Wearing heavy utility gloves all day
options.B: Frequent and proper hand hygiene
options.C: Administering prophylactic antibiotics
options.D: Changing bed linens every morning

explanation: Never underestimate the power of clean hands! Good hand hygiene washes away transient germs before they can travel from patient to patient.

question: A nurse manager refuses to share a patient's secret diagnosis, believing that keeping confidentiality is a universal moral rule no matter what. Which theory is this?

options.A: Utilitarianism
options.B: Systems theory
options.C: Scientific management
options.D: Deontology

explanation: Deontology is all about strict moral duties and rules ("doing the right thing because it's your duty"), no matter what the outcome might be.

question: Where do water-soluble nutrients go right after crossing the intestinal wall?

options.A: Upward into the lungs to assist with oxygen exchange
options.B: Directly into the urinary bladder for quick disposal
options.C: Into the portal circulation straight to the liver
options.D: Directly to the skin surface for temperature control

explanation: You're doing great! Water-soluble nutrients take a direct trip through the portal vein to the liver, where they get filtered and prepped for the rest of the body.

question: Why might a multi-million-dollar MRI machine be considered inappropriate technology for a rural primary health clinic?

options.A: Rural patients do not have brains or spinal cords to scan
options.B: Magnetic machines are forbidden by traditional cultural beliefs
options.C: The clinic lacks reliable electricity, trained technicians, and repair parts
options.D: The government prefers traditional herbs over digital imaging

explanation: Advanced machinery fails the test of appropriateness if the local setting lacks the infrastructure and support to keep it running. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h6)

question: Two clinical supervisors watch the same nursing student perform a procedure and grade them using the same checklist. What are they checking?

options.A: Test-retest validity
options.B: Content consistency
options.C: Inter-rater reliability
options.D: Patient satisfaction

explanation: Inter-rater reliability checks whether different observers get similar scores when using the exact same tool. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h7)

question: A pregnant woman asks why she needs more fruit servings now. What is the best response?

options.A: Eating more fruit is only needed to prevent weight loss in the third trimester.
options.B: You must replace all your meals with fresh fruit juices during pregnancy.
options.C: Your body needs higher vitamins and fiber to support increased metabolic demands and growth.
options.D: Pregnancy completely stops your body from absorbing vitamins from regular food.

explanation: Well done! Pregnancy is a time of double duty—maternal tissues and the growing baby both need extra vitamins and fiber.

question: Why is it dangerous for a patient to rub their eye right after getting a numbing (anesthetic) drop?

options.A: Rubbing forces the medication deep into the tear ducts
options.B: Friction triggers an immediate severe allergy
options.C: Pressure changes will rupture internal blood vessels
options.D: They can scratch their cornea without feeling the pain

explanation: Numbing drops take away pain sensation temporarily. If the patient rubs their eye hard, they could easily scratch the delicate tissue and won't even feel it happening!

question: Which imaging test uses contrast dye and X-rays to clearly view the inside of the uterus and fallopian tubes?

options.A: Transvaginal ultrasound
options.B: Saline infusion sonohysterography
options.C: Hysterosalpingography
options.D: Abdominal CT scan

explanation: Correct! Hysterosalpingography (HSG) combines 'hystero' (uterus), 'salpingo' (tubes), and 'graphy' (imaging) using dye to see if the tubes are open.

question: What is the very first sign of a pressure sore starting to form?

options.A: A deep open crater with exposed subcutaneous fat
options.B: A fluid-filled blister with dark purple discoloration
options.C: Complete skin death with black dry eschar
options.D: Non-blanching erythema over a bony prominence

explanation: Well done! If skin stays red and doesn't turn white when you press it over a bone, pressure damage is starting.

question: How do association areas differ from sensory and motor areas in the brain?

options.A: They directly connect spinal nerves to peripheral skeletal muscles
options.B: They are located exclusively deep within the brain stem rather than the cortex
options.C: They only function during deep sleep and remain completely inactive while awake
options.D: They deal with complex thoughts and reasoning rather than direct input or output

explanation: Think of association areas as the brain's processing hubs—they bring different pieces of information together for high-level thinking and reasoning!

question: An older adult with low vision is going home from the clinic. What is the most important home safety tip to give them?

options.A: Keep all windows covered to block glaring sunlight
options.B: Paint all interior walls a bright, shiny white
options.C: Improve indoor lighting and clear away tripping hazards like loose rugs
options.D: Install tinted glass windows throughout the house

explanation: Good lighting helps them make the absolute most of their remaining sight, and clearing out clutter keeps them safe from nasty falls.

question: Which type of hospital waste must always be destroyed using high-temperature incineration?

options.A: Anatomical and pathological waste
options.B: Used office paper and administrative files
options.C: Non-contaminated cardboard delivery boxes
options.D: Empty intravenous fluid glass bottles

explanation: Human tissues and body parts must be completely incinerated for sanitary and cultural reasons. You're building great clinical habits!

question: Why does the body's immune system attack mismatched blood?

options.A: It tries to repair the damaged cells using white blood cells
options.B: It recognizes the foreign antigens as nonself and makes antibodies
options.C: It runs out of normal plasma proteins to handle the extra fluid
options.D: It mistakes the red blood cells for harmful bacteria

explanation: You've got this! The immune system's main job is spotting foreign invaders. When it sees unfamiliar antigens on donated red blood cells, it treats them as dangerous and attacks. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h1)

question: In nursing, what is the golden rule regarding documentation?

options.A: It cost no money to execute
options.B: It legally never happened
options.C: It was performed perfectly
options.D: It was done by a doctor instead

explanation: Remember this rule always! Courts and professional boards only trust written notes. If it's not documented, legally, it was never done.

question: What are the two main systems combined within the genito-urinary tract?

options.A: The nervous and skeletal systems
options.B: The digestive and endocrine systems
options.C: The respiratory and circulatory systems
options.D: The urinary and reproductive systems

explanation: The genito-urinary system is a combination of the urinary tract organs and the reproductive organs due to their close developmental and physical links. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T1#GNS213_U4_T1_h1)

question: What term describes the dangerous point where two or more organ systems fail during severe, prolonged shock?

options.A: Multiple Organ Dysfunction Syndrome
options.B: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation
options.C: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
options.D: Systemic Vascular Resistance Failure

explanation: MODS is what happens when severe shock goes on too long unchecked: the whole body cascade causes organs like the kidneys, lungs, and liver to start shutting down one by one.

question: How do incident reporting systems help a hospital protect itself legally?

options.A: By ensuring nurses never have to document clinical procedures again
options.B: By identifying clinical system failures early so corrective action can be taken
options.C: By transferring all blame directly to the state ministry of health
options.D: By automatically hiding medical errors from patient legal representatives

explanation: Incident reports catch safety gaps early so management can fix them before they turn into major lawsuits and patient harm.

question: A patient recovering from an MVA suddenly complains of dizziness, looks pale, and her pulse drops. What is the nurse's best immediate action?

options.A: Elevate the patient's legs and monitor vital signs
options.B: Take her to the operating room for an emergency laparotomy
options.C: Administer a strong dose of oral antibiotics
options.D: Tell her to stand up and walk around to improve circulation

explanation: Elevating the legs helps blood return to the brain during a vasovagal episode, quickly relieving dizziness and fainting symptoms. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h7)

question: What is the main reason healthcare workers should NOT recap needles after giving an injection?

options.A: It is the leading cause of accidental needle-stick injuries
options.B: It wastes valuable clinic time during busy immunizations
options.C: It makes the safety box fill up much faster than normal
options.D: It breaks the plunger inside the plastic syringe barrel

explanation: Trying to recap needles often leads to accidental punctures to the fingers and hands of the nurse. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h7)

question: Why does milk make it so easy for bacteria to grow quickly?

options.A: It is usually stored in open containers in the market
options.B: It undergoes heavy chemical processing before packaging
options.C: It contains a high concentration of essential nutrients
options.D: It is naturally warm and has a very low pH level

explanation: Spot on! Milk is packed with proteins, fats, and sugars, which makes it a rich food source for microorganisms to feed and multiply on.

question: What is the main sign of neurasthenia?

options.A: Chronic nervous exhaustion and physical fatigue
options.B: Permanent neurological nerve damage
options.C: Sudden episodes of complete muscle paralysis
options.D: Severe cognitive decline and memory loss

explanation: You've got this! Neurasthenia is simply known as a condition of ongoing physical tiredness and nervous burnout. Keep up the great work!

question: What is the term for accidental, uncontrolled cell death that spills cell contents and causes inflammation?

options.A: Apoptosis
options.B: Atrophy
options.C: Necrosis
options.D: Hyperplasia

explanation: Necrosis is messy, accidental cell death from severe injury. Because the cell bursts open, it triggers local inflammation.

question: Which of these is NOT a primary goal of pharmacovigilance?

options.A: Minimizing risks associated with pharmaceutical products
options.B: Promoting the safe and rational use of medicines
options.C: Guarantees that a marketed drug will never cause any side effects
options.D: Contributing to the assessment of drug benefits and harms

explanation: You got it! No drug system can promise zero side effects because all strong medicines carry some level of risk.

question: How do nurses use prevalence data when seeking funding from health ministries?

options.A: To demonstrate the total burden of disease and justify resource requests
options.B: To calculate the exact birth date of every infected community member
options.C: To replace physical examinations during routine home visits
options.D: To prove that no further medical supplies are required in the region

explanation: Showing the total number of people affected helps justify why funding and materials are urgently required. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h6)

question: What is a heartbreaking result of unwanted pregnancies in places where safe care isn't available?

options.A: Guaranteed delivery of healthy twins
options.B: Automatic enrollment in advanced academic scholarships
options.C: Immediate maternal immunity against infectious diseases
options.D: Unsafe abortions leading to severe infection and bleeding

explanation: When women lack access to safe options, they often resort to dangerous procedures that cause terrible injuries and loss of life.

question: What does 'clinical significance' mean in simple terms when looking at drug research?

options.A: Whether the research paper was published in an international journal
options.B: Whether the study results make a meaningful, noticeable difference to the patient's health
options.C: Whether the pharmaceutical company made a profit from the drug trial
options.D: Whether the mathematical formula used in the data analysis was complex enough

explanation: Well done! Numbers might show a tiny statistical change, but clinical significance means the patient actually feels or gets better in real life.

question: What is a helpful nursing action to ease a patient's anxiety about being stuck in traction?

options.A: Explain the equipment clearly and keep their call bell close by
options.B: Take away all entertainment to help them sleep
options.C: Promise to take the traction off whenever they get bored
options.D: Tell family members not to visit so the room stays quiet

explanation: You've got this! Knowing how the equipment works and knowing help is just a button press away builds huge trust and comfort for the patient.

question: Which of the following interventions requires skilled nursing rather than basic custodial care?

options.A: Helping a client put on a shirt and button up the front
options.B: Walking beside an elderly client to prevent a fall in the hallway
options.C: Cutting meat into small pieces on a plate during lunch
options.D: Changing a complex surgical wound dressing and monitoring an IV line

explanation: Wound dressings and intravenous lines are clinical medical procedures that require the expertise of a skilled nurse. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h3)

question: Which nursing action directly supports antimicrobial stewardship?

options.A: Advocating to collect culture specimens before starting antibiotics
options.B: Giving leftover antibiotics to a family member with a cold
options.C: Requesting broad-spectrum drugs for every routine fever
options.D: Stopping antibiotic therapy as soon as mild symptoms improve

explanation: Getting cultures first ensures the right targeted drug is used, preventing unnecessary use of broad-spectrum medications. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h4)

question: A patient loves sweets and is struggling to cut them out completely. What is a smart, gradual first goal?

options.A: Buying expensive sugar-free substitutes from abroad
options.B: Stopping all sugar consumption immediately today
options.C: Replacing sugary snacks with fruit on alternate days
options.D: Ignoring the sweet intake until the next hospital visit

explanation: You're thinking like a pro nurse! Small, baby steps are way easier for patients to stick with than sudden, impossible restrictions. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h5)

question: What is the most important infection control practice for a family caregiver managing a home gastrostomy tube?

options.A: Boiling all feeding bags in water after every single meal
options.B: Performing thorough hand hygiene before handling the tube
options.C: Cleaning the entire feeding pump machine with bleach daily
options.D: Wearing sterile surgical gloves for every single water flush

explanation: Proper handwashing is the single most effective way to prevent harmful bacteria from entering the gastrostomy site or formula bag. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT typically evaluated during a standard newborn Apgar check?

options.A: Blood glucose level
options.B: Muscle tone
options.C: Skin color
options.D: Heart rate

explanation: The Apgar score assesses appearance, pulse, grimace, activity, and respiration; blood glucose is a lab test, not an Apgar parameter. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h6)

question: Why must a community diagnosis look at factors like housing and clean water?

options.A: These environmental factors directly shape the health outcomes of the population
options.B: Building codes are the legal responsibility of public health nurses
options.C: Hospital administrators require these statistics for annual budgeting
options.D: Doctors use these details to prescribe specific pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Health is influenced by social, economic, and environmental conditions, not just medical care alone. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why does a patient with severe anemia often have a fast heartbeat (tachycardia)?

options.A: The lungs stop absorbing carbon dioxide properly
options.B: Blood vessels become strictly constricted throughout the body
options.C: White blood cells are attacking the heart muscle tissue
options.D: The heart pumps faster to make up for low oxygen carrying capacity

explanation: When red blood cells are low, your body doesn't get enough oxygen. To help out, the heart beats faster to pump the remaining cells around the body quicker. You've got this!

question: Why is it important for nurses to ask about cultural beliefs regarding medicines?

options.A: It allows the nurse to legally rewrite hospital medication formularies
options.B: It replaces the need to check laboratory blood test results in the ward
options.C: It ensures the hospital receives international funding for traditional research
options.D: It helps uncover hidden practices that might affect how the patient takes prescribed drugs

explanation: Understanding cultural perspectives reveals compliance barriers and concurrent therapies that patients might not otherwise mention. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h5)

question: A nurse classifies patient satisfaction scores as 'poor', 'fair', or 'good'. Which level of measurement is this?

options.A: Nominal
options.B: Ordinal
options.C: Ratio
options.D: Interval

explanation: Satisfaction grades have a logical order from poor to good, making them ordinal data, though the distance between the grades is not mathematically fixed. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T1#GNS224_U2_T1_h3)

question: A pregnant mum taking daily iron pills complains of severe constipation. What is the main reason behind this?

options.A: Iron vitamins cause the stomach to shrink in size
options.B: Iron instantly stops the production of all digestive juices
options.C: Excess iron unabsorbed in the gut binds and hardens the stool
options.D: Iron forces the body to expel water through the skin instead

explanation: Well thought out! The iron that the body doesn't absorb interacts inside the gut, turning the waste firmer and harder to pass.

question: What is a key physical sign that a patient is feeling very stressed?

options.A: Relaxed facial muscles
options.B: Calm and steady posture
options.C: Deep, slow breathing
options.D: Pacing and restlessness

explanation: When the 'fight-or-flight' response kicks in, people often find it hard to sit still, resulting in fidgeting, pacing, or jittery movements.

question: An examiner is preparing to look at a patient's left eye using a direct ophthalmoscope. Which setup is correct?

options.A: Stand directly behind the patient and use both eyes at once
options.B: Rest the scope firmly against the bridge of the patient's nose
options.C: Hold the scope in the left hand and use the left eye
options.D: Hold the scope in the right hand and use the left eye

explanation: Using matching sides (left hand and left eye for the patient's left eye) allows the examiner to get close without colliding with the patient. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h6)

question: What usually happens to a community of solution once the problem they faced is completely fixed?

options.A: The group may naturally dissolve or end its activities
options.B: It transforms into a permanent territorial government
options.C: The members stop speaking to each other forever
options.D: The members are legally forced to relocate to a city

explanation: Correct! Since they gathered for a specific mission, they often wrap things up and disband once the job is done.

question: A woman at 36 weeks pregnant with twins asks for a home birth. What should you, as her midwife, do?

options.A: Delay the decision until labor pain actually starts
options.B: Approve the home birth due to normal pregnancy progress
options.C: Deny the request because multiple gestation and preterm status increase risk
options.D: Accept her only if she promises to push quickly

explanation: Twins and early babies (before 37 weeks) need hospital facilities just in case they need extra help. Home birth isn't safe for them.

question: When does the second stage of labor end?

options.A: At the onset of true contractions
options.B: When the cervix is fully dilated
options.C: At the birth of the baby
options.D: When the placenta is delivered

explanation: The second stage spans from full cervical dilation all the way until the infant is completely delivered. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h3)

question: How should you write five-tenths as a decimal to avoid a dangerous dosing error?
explanation: Always put a leading zero before the decimal point (0.5 instead of .5). If you miss the dot on '.5', it looks like 5—and that's a massive overdose!

question: Why must everyone in a household get treated at the same time if one person has pinworms?

options.A: Untreated relatives will develop severe liver failure within forty-eight hours
options.B: Family members share identical genetic susceptibility to roundworm larvae
options.C: Single treatments are legally prohibited for treating minor household pests
options.D: Pinworms spread rapidly among family members through silent reinfection cycles

explanation: Pinworms spread so easily at home. If you only treat one person, everyone else passes the worms right back to them!

question: What is the main purpose of the thick mucus layer inside your stomach?

options.A: To protect the stomach tissue from its own acid and enzymes
options.B: To activate pepsinogen into working pepsin
options.C: To help move food quickly into the small intestine
options.D: To absorb vitamin B12 directly into the bloodstream

explanation: Since stomach acid is strong enough to break down food, that thick mucus layer acts like a shield so the stomach doesn't digest itself!

question: As a community health nurse, what is a key duty when preparing for disasters?

options.A: Breaking down emergency guidelines into simple steps for residents
options.B: Managing the national budget for disaster relief
options.C: Building storm shelters and reinforced concrete walls
options.D: Declaring a formal state of emergency in the region

explanation: Great job! Nurses act as a bridge, turning complex disaster plans into clear, everyday steps that everyone can easily follow.

question: What is the primary purpose of establishing a referral pathway for home delivery?

options.A: Complying with hospital decoration rules
options.B: Reducing the cost of antenatal drugs
options.C: Ensuring fast transfer to a hospital if complications occur
options.D: Giving the nurse time to rest during labor

explanation: A referral pathway guarantees that the patient can be moved smoothly to a higher level of care without unnecessary delay. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h7)

question: Which question best reflects the true spirit of a Root Cause Analysis?

options.A: Why did the patient choose to visit our hospital for treatment?
options.B: Why did the system workflow allow this safety barrier to fail?
options.C: How many disciplinary strikes does this worker have on file?
options.D: Which staff member failed to follow our strict hospital rules?

explanation: You got it! RCA focuses entirely on fixing broken processes rather than pointing fingers at individuals.

question: Which hormone tells the bone marrow to make more red blood cells during pregnancy?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Erythropoietin
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: Erythropoietin is like a special chemical messenger released by the kidneys to tell the bone marrow, 'Hey, we need more red blood cells for the baby!'

question: What keeps a polyvalent nurse eager to keep learning on the job?

options.A: The desire to become a hospital administrator eventually
options.B: The need to maintain skills across many different medical fields
options.C: Pressure from hospital managers to reduce operating costs
options.D: Strict government laws requiring annual license renewals

explanation: Well done! Since they work in diverse units, polyvalent nurses always stay on their toes, updating their knowledge across multiple specialties.

question: Which payment method is most likely to push a family into sudden poverty during a major illness?

options.A: General government revenue
options.B: International donor grants
options.C: Mandatory health insurance
options.D: Out-of-pocket payments

explanation: When there is no insurance to fall back on, paying cash directly for major treatments can easily wipe out a family's entire life savings overnight.

question: What is the best way for a nurse to find out a patient's specific religious dietary needs?

options.A: Review only standard laboratory blood test results
options.B: Ask open-ended questions during the admission interview
options.C: Guess based on the patient's country of origin
options.D: Wait for the patient to complain about hospital food

explanation: Never guess! Asking respectful, open-ended questions during admission helps us avoid assumptions and get accurate info on what our patients need.

question: Which body measurement is most commonly used in the community to quickly screen young children for severe malnutrition?

options.A: Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC)
options.B: Total body surface area
options.C: Waist-to-hip ratio
options.D: Head circumference

explanation: The MUAC tape is a nurse's best friend during community outreaches—it's fast, easy, and great for checking young children on the spot!

question: What is the core message of the contingency approach to management?

options.A: Every hospital must use the exact same leadership rules
options.B: Financial incentives are the only way to motivate staff
options.C: Managers should never change their personal leadership style
options.D: The best management style depends on the specific situation

explanation: Contingency theory teaches that leaders must adapt their approach based on the unique demands of each scenario. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h5)

question: What happens to a blood pressure reading if you use a cuff that is way too narrow for the patient's arm?

options.A: The reading will be falsely high
options.B: The blood pressure cannot be measured at all
options.C: The reading will be falsely low
options.D: The reading will remain completely normal

explanation: A narrow cuff needs extra squeeze to block the artery in a bigger arm, which tricks the machine or gauge into showing a falsely high reading. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h5)

question: What does the term 'intersectionality' mean in healthcare?

options.A: The intersection of rural roads leading to a clinic
options.B: A meeting point between doctors and community leaders
options.C: How gender overlaps with poverty, age, and disability
options.D: The physical crossing of blood vessels in the heart

explanation: Intersectionality simply means looking at the whole person—how things like gender, age, and poverty combine to create unique challenges. Great concept to know as a nurse!

question: What is the correct order of steps in a PDSA quality cycle?

options.A: Prepare, Design, Survey, Assess
options.B: Plan, Do, Study, Act
options.C: Predict, Document, Solve, Apply
options.D: Prioritize, Delegate, Supervise, Audit

explanation: Spot on! PDSA stands for Plan, Do, Study, Act. It’s your trusty roadmap for testing small changes on the ward step by step.

question: What naturally happens to serum albumin levels when a patient's body goes through sudden inflammation?

options.A: They remain unchanged
options.B: They increase
options.C: They decrease
options.D: They fluctuate wildly

explanation: Albumin is known as a negative acute-phase reactant. When inflammation flares up, the liver slows down albumin production—good to keep in mind!

question: Why must older adults or heart patients start levothyroxine at a very low dose?

options.A: Because high initial doses cause permanent damage to the thyroid gland
options.B: To prevent sudden increases in metabolic demand that could stress the heart
options.C: Because older adults absorb the medication much faster than young adults
options.D: To prevent the kidneys from excreting the drug before it works

explanation: Revving up the body's metabolism too fast is like slamming the gas pedal in an old car—it puts too much strain on the heart and can trigger chest pain.

question: If a factory worker's liver enzymes are overactive due to chemical exposure, what usually happens to their regular medications?

options.A: The drugs will instantly crystallize inside the stomach lining
options.B: The drugs will turn into harmless vitamins inside the bloodstream
options.C: The drugs will remain active inside the body for many extra weeks
options.D: The drugs may break down too fast and lose their therapeutic effect

explanation: When liver enzymes are in overdrive, they clear out medications too quickly. This means the drug leaves the body before it even has a chance to help the patient! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h4)

question: In home health nursing, who do we consider as the whole 'unit of care'?

options.A: The entire local community council
options.B: The attending physician and nurse
options.C: The patient and their family together
options.D: The patient isolated from relatives

explanation: Spot on! At home, we treat the patient and their family as one team because family members play a huge role in recovery.

question: What is the appropriate action for a general nurse when a patient requires highly specialized medical nutrition therapy for a rare metabolic disease?

options.A: Refer the patient to a registered dietitian or specialist
options.B: Ignore the condition since nutrition is not a nursing concern
options.C: Guess the correct nutrient formula and prescribe it immediately
options.D: Discharge the patient to avoid having to deal with the complexity

explanation: Nurses must recognize their scope of practice and collaborate by referring complex cases to experts like dietitians. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h4)

question: What do we call the recovery period right after a seizure?

options.A: The permanent damage caused by fits
options.B: The exact moment a seizure begins
options.C: The recovery period right after a seizure
options.D: A test used to diagnose epilepsy

explanation: That phase right after a fit is called the postictal state. The brain is basically resting and resetting, which is why your patient might wake up feeling super tired or confused.

question: An emergency ward is trying out a new documentation tool. What action will best help the staff adopt it successfully?

options.A: Forcing staff to use the exact original tool without listening to their feedback
options.B: Hiding the tool instructions until every nurse has completed a written exam
options.C: Allowing the emergency nurses to adapt the tool slightly to fit their fast-paced workflow
options.D: Punishing any nurse who forgets to use the tool during the first week

explanation: Flexibility is key! When staff get to shape how a tool fits their busy shift, they feel proud and are much more likely to use it.

question: How does the myelin coating affect the speed of an electrical signal traveling down a nerve fiber?

options.A: It increases impulse speed via saltatory conduction
options.B: It has no effect on nerve conduction velocity
options.C: It stops the impulse entirely until it reaches a synapse
options.D: It slows impulse speed by creating resistance

explanation: Myelin acts like insulation on an electrical wire. It lets the signal jump rapidly from one node to the next, speeding things up tremendously!

question: A 12-year-old child is brought to the clinic for repeatedly skipping school and running away. How should you as a nurse classify these actions?

options.A: Adult felonies
options.B: Violent offenses
options.C: Property offenses
options.D: Status offenses

explanation: Easy and clear! Skipping school and running away are classic status offenses because adults wouldn't face criminal charges for doing the exact same thing.

question: A modern nurse researcher studying how telehealth apps improve blood pressure control in rural communities is demonstrating which current trend?

options.A: Abandoning clinical practice for pure laboratory biology
options.B: Integrating technology into nursing care solutions
options.C: Returning to early twentieth-century hospital routines
options.D: Relying exclusively on 19th-century sanitary data

explanation: Modern nursing science actively investigates digital health tools like telehealth to extend quality care to remote populations. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why do nurses apply a cotton stockinette and padding before wrapping the plaster rolls?

options.A: To add bright color and decoration to the finished cast
options.B: To help the wet plaster dry much faster from the inside
options.C: To protect the underlying skin from irritation and pressure
options.D: To prevent the limb from shrinking inside the hard cast

explanation: Padding acts as a cozy cushion between the hard plaster and bony areas, keeping the skin safe from sores.

question: A patient is brought to the clinic by their adult child and seems a bit confused. What should you make sure to note about their background info?

options.A: The demographic profile using entirely estimated clinical values
options.B: The source of history as a family member rather than the patient
options.C: The child's personal medical history instead of the patient's data
options.D: The patient as an unreliable historian without further explanation

explanation: Spot on! Always write down who gave the information so the next nurse knows whether it came directly from the patient or a family member.

question: Which process is safe to use directly on living human skin?

options.A: High-level disinfection
options.B: Sterilization
options.C: Incineration
options.D: Antisepsis

explanation: Antiseptics are formulated to be gentle on living skin. Strong sterilizing chemicals would cause chemical burns, ouch!

question: What common fungal mouth infection often pops up when an HIV patient's immune system drops?

options.A: Oral candidiasis (thrush)
options.B: Salivary gland stones
options.C: Gingival hyperplasia
options.D: Dental caries

explanation: Oral candidiasis (thrush) loves to appear in the mouth when immune defenses are low. Easy spot!

question: In research, what do we call the 'Hawthorne effect'?

options.A: Patients refusing to give consent for data collection in the ward
options.B: Data getting lost because field notes were not written down promptly
options.C: The researcher missing key events due to fatigue during a long shift
options.D: People changing their behavior because they know they are being watched

explanation: Spot on! The Hawthorne effect happens naturally because humans tend to act differently when they realize someone is watching them.

question: What is a very common emotional experience for patients facing the end of their lives?

options.A: Existential distress and questioning life meaning
options.B: An intense desire to run marathons
options.C: Complete indifference to surroundings and people
options.D: Sudden loss of all emotional feelings

explanation: You got it! Toward the end of life, it's completely normal for patients to look back, wonder about their life's purpose, and work through big deep questions.

question: Which of the following is a fat-soluble vitamin?

options.A: Vitamin A
options.B: Folic acid
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Vitamin B12

explanation: Vitamins A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble and can be stored in body fat, unlike the water-soluble B and C vitamins. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T9#GNS215_U6_T9_h2)

question: A female patient arrives at the clinic with a fractured wrist and several bruises on her torso. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Confront the accompanying partner aggressively to demand an explanation
options.B: Document the injuries as accidental falls without questioning further
options.C: Provide necessary medical treatment while ensuring a safe, private space to talk
options.D: Discharge the patient quickly before the partner becomes impatient

explanation: Treating immediate physical needs while offering privacy and a supportive atmosphere helps build trust for potential disclosure. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h2)

question: Why is it important for nurses in Nigeria to ask patients about any traditional herbal remedies they might be taking?

options.A: Traditional herbs are scientifically proven to cure type 1 diabetes permanently
options.B: Herbal products completely replace the need for blood glucose monitoring
options.C: Traditional remedies have no chemical impact on human liver enzymes
options.D: Herbal mixtures can interact with prescribed drugs and cause unexpected blood sugar drops

explanation: Spot on! Many local herbal preparations can unexpectedly drop blood sugar levels, leading to severe hypoglycaemia when mixed with regular diabetes medications.

question: What do we call a host where a parasite or pathogen grows up and reproduces?

options.A: An organism where the infectious agent reaches maturity and reproduces
options.B: An organism that can catch an infection but never pass it on
options.C: An environmental source where bacteria live without growing
options.D: An insect that only carries a virus on its outer legs

explanation: This is known as the definitive host. It's the place where the pathogen finally grows into its adult, reproductive stage.

question: What do we call the routine choices you make using already established hospital rules and procedures?

options.A: Non-programmed choices
options.B: Programmed choices
options.C: Operational choices
options.D: Strategic choices

explanation: Programmed choices are your go-to solutions for familiar, everyday situations where a clear hospital guideline already exists.

question: Which of these is NOT a perk of using mucous membrane drug routes?

options.A: Bypassing harsh gastrointestinal fluids
options.B: Rapid entry into the bloodstream
options.C: Slowest possible onset of drug action
options.D: Usefulness for vomiting patients

explanation: Quite the opposite! Because mucous membranes are packed with blood vessels, they usually give a very fast onset of action, not a slow one.

question: Which brain structure forms the roof at the back of the fourth ventricle?

options.A: Pituitary gland
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Frontal cortex
options.D: Olfactory bulb

explanation: Correct! The fourth ventricle sits right in front of the cerebellum, which forms its lovely protective roof at the back.

question: Why is it wonderful to let a patient pick out their own clothes for the day?

options.A: It saves time during morning care
options.B: It matches hospital uniform rules
options.C: It builds personal dignity and self-esteem
options.D: It keeps the clothes clean longer

explanation: Spot on! Small choices like picking an outfit give patients back control and boost their mood all day long.

question: Why is cerebral palsy described as a non-progressive condition?

options.A: Symptoms always improve steadily without any medical care
options.B: Treatment can completely repair the damaged brain tissue
options.C: The original brain injury does not get worse over time
options.D: The child will eventually outgrow all physical symptoms

explanation: While the physical body changes and challenges may evolve as a child grows, the underlying brain damage remains static. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is the most common reason a breastfeeding mother develops sore and cracked nipples?

options.A: Normal hormonal fluctuations
options.B: Incorrect infant latching technique
options.C: Excessive production of oxytocin
options.D: Wearing a supportive cotton bra

explanation: A poor latch is usually the culprit behind nipple pain. Helping the mother adjust how the baby latches makes a world of difference!

question: Which of the following is a common misconception about dominant genetic disorders that nurses often correct?

options.A: Lifestyle changes can completely erase a faulty gene
options.B: Genetic conditions never show up in families twice
options.C: Every child of an affected parent will automatically inherit the disease
options.D: Genetic disorders only affect elderly individuals

explanation: With autosomal dominant conditions, each pregnancy carries a specific probability, such as fifty percent, rather than an absolute certainty for every single child. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h3)

question: Why do mental health diagnostic manuals keep getting updated?

options.A: To make nursing documentation twice as long to complete
options.B: To reflect new research and changing scientific understanding
options.C: To increase the total number of medications manufacturers sell
options.D: To erase all past history of psychiatric care

explanation: Science never stops growing! As we discover more about the human mind, manuals are updated so your nursing care stays top-notch.

question: Why is passive immunity considered temporary?

options.A: Vaccines prevent passive antibodies from staying in the bloodstream
options.B: The immune system destroys the transferred antibodies immediately
options.C: Maternal antibodies are blocked by the infant's stomach acid
options.D: The body does not manufacture its own memory cells or antibodies
